ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, including beneficial ownership transparency requirements; Corporate Registry Act (Alberta); FINTRAC regulations and guidance under the PCMLTFA; and OSFI-issued AML/CFT directives applicable to regulated entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copy of passport or national identity document for each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in an apostille-country; otherwise consular legalization by the issuing country's embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of good standing / corporate status certificate for any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or equivalent registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with sworn English translation if not already in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized consent to act as director (Form 4 or equivalent under the Alberta Business Corporations Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each proposed director executing before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / proof of source of funds for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization; must be in English or French

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and signing authorities against: (1) the consolidated Canadian sanctions list administered by Global Affairs Canada and the Public Safety Canada listings; (2) United Nations Security Council (UNSC) consolidated list; (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (4) Interpol-issued notices and Canadian Police Information Centre (CPIC); and (5) FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs) of domestic and foreign origin. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP status, including potential misuse of corporate vehicles; screening must be completed before incorporation filing and recorded in the corporation's AML/KYC file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via Service Alberta authorized service providers using the Corporate Registry System (CORES)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French form, using Latin alphabetic characters; names in any other script must be transliterated into Latin characters and must be pronounceable. The name must be distinctive as determined by the NUANS preliminary name search, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name or reserved name under section 11 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a corporate name, the applicant or its counsel may file a written administrative review request with the Alberta Registrar of Corporations through the CORES service provider, within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must attach the original NUANS report, grounds for distinction, and any supporting legal or public-interest argument. The Registrar will issue a written decision. If the decision remains adverse, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. Alternatively, a new name search and reservation may be filed immediately without loss of the incorporation workflow.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk marketplace FBA business, provided that the virtual office offers a physical street address in Alberta, does not rely solely on a post-office box, and can accept service of process and mail forwarding during business hours. Service providers operating a physical reception and mail-handling facility are acceptable under Sections 8 and 9 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated under 5% per annum for an ISIC 4791 low-risk cross-border e-commerce operation. Unannounced physical inspection is unlikely unless AML/CFT red flags are triggered or the Canada Revenue Agency initiates a compliance verification; documentary and electronic reviews remain the typical enforcement method.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, incorporating the core corporate formation provisions governing corporate name, articles of incorporation, registration, certificate of incorporation, first directors, by-laws, registered office, share issuance, corporate records, and annual maintenance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), Government of Alberta; online filings through Corporate Registry Online.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Business Corporation Act registry form) and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the ABCA; no escrow account is mandated. The incorporator defines the authorized share capital in the articles either with or without par value, and shares may be issued for cash, property, or past services as set by the directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED at the first board meeting that the share subscription agreements submitted are accepted; the directors are authorized to issue, allot and record the subscribed shares in the share register under the Articles of Incorporation. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office is fixed in Alberta at the address in the Notice of Registered Office and [Agent Name] is appointed as registered agent for service. FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed President/CEO, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements and perfect corporate filings under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (through authorized NUANS service providers; online Corporate Registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary search to verify the proposed corporate name is distinctive and not confusingly similar. Submit a corporate name reservation application online or in writing; pay the reservation fee; obtain the Name Reservation Report valid for 90 days. The proposed name must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Incorporated or Limited.
required_dossiers: Consent to use names or letters, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusing, file a new reservation with a distinctive suffix or prefix, or request reconsideration with consent letters from the prior user. A refiled NUANS request usually cures the objection within one additional business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Registrar of Companies via Corporate Registry Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Alberta Articles of Incorporation form, setting out the corporate name, registered office street address, share structure, restrictions, number of directors and first directors' names. Have the articles executed by the incorporator and file electronically. Attach all required consents and pay the prescribed filing fee. Retain the e-filing acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as First Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a refusal or query, review the objection, amend the articles where permitted, and refile. Submit executed consents and updated name reservation within the statutory response period; a legal cure may be effected by amended articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Registrar of Companies (electronic certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registrar processes the filed articles and fee, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the Corporate Registry online portal. Record the Corporate Access Number and corporate status; the certificate is conclusive proof of incorporation. File the certificate in the corporate minute book and make a certified copy for banking and CRA registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or Corporate Access Number is not generated within the service standard, contact Corporate Registry to verify submission; a certified duplicate may be requested if the electronic certificate is misplaced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-laws, Registered Office and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary of the Corporation; filings with Alberta Corporate Registry if registered office or director information changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the by-laws; issue shares; appoint officers; confirm the registered office address and appoint a registered agent for service; open bank accounts; and authorize negotiation of Amazon FBA agreements. Record all proceedings in the minute book, sign share certificates, and file any prescribed notices if the initial articles did not fully record all appointments.
required_dossiers: Notice of First Meeting or Unanimous Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is identified, ratify the action by a supplemental unanimous resolution, waive notice in writing, or file amended articles or notices with the Registry. Most organizational defects can be cured retroactively under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online; Alberta Finance via CRA secured services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access Business Registration Online; enter the Corporate Access Number and legal name; register for the Business Number, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, payroll account if employees, and import/export account if cross-border trade. Provide the NAICS code 454110 and describe the Amazon FBA marketplace retail activity. Retain the confirmation notice.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
Corporate address and legal name details
Description of principal business activity (Amazon FBA retail)
Bank account details for tax remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the enrollment is rejected or an account is not activated, contact the CRA business inquiries line, correct any name or address mismatch, and request a letter of confirmation. Provide the Certificate of Incorporation and a signed authorization if a Business Number is missing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable Alberta municipal authority, e.g., City of Calgary Licensing or City of Edmonton Business Licencing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the municipal business licence by-law requires a general business licence for online-only retailers operating from the registered office or home office. Submit a business licence application with the municipal licensing body and pay the applicable fee if the activity constitutes a business within the municipality. For Amazon FBA virtual operations, obtain a written exemption confirmation if the municipality certifies that no physical presence triggers licensing.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office or lease
Zoning or home occupation approval if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is denied due to zoning or by-law requirements, request a variance, home-based business permit, or written exemption letter. Appeal the denial to the municipal licence appeal committee within the prescribed period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial manufacturing licence in Alberta is required for ISIC 4791 retail sale via internet (Amazon FBA general) because the activity does not involve manufacturing or physical production within the province.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no provincial operating or manufacturing permit is compulsory for pure online retail through a marketplace; a general municipal business licence or home occupation permit may be required by local by-laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full Environmental Impact Assessment triggered under the Environmental Assessment Regulation because the activity is non-manufacturing, warehouse operations are managed by Amazon FBA, and no ground-disturbing operations occur in Alberta.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds apply. General waste management obligations, including packaging diversion and disposal, lie primarily with Amazon FBA and downstream logistics; the merchant must ensure product packaging and batteries comply with applicable federal and provincial environmental requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defence or fire-safety certificate is required for a virtual office. If the registered office is a physical office, Alberta OHS and the local fire authority may require workplace fire-safety inspections and building occupancy approvals. Maintain an emergency response protocol and comply with landlord fire safety requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; Business Registration Online (BRO) portal at canada.ca/business-registration; ongoing account administration via CRA My Business Account (MyBA) for GST/HST returns and correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation obtains a 9-digit Business Number (BN) plus a GST/HST program account (RT prefix) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or, for non-residents, Form RC1A (Request for GST/HST Registration of a Non-Resident), submitted electronically through BRO or by mail to the CRA Sudbury Tax Centre. Required particulars: certified certificate of incorporation or foreign equivalent, registered office address in Canada or agency address, full director/officer list, anticipated Canadian taxable revenue (CAD 30,000 threshold analysis), high-level business activity description (NAICS/ISIC mapping), and appointment of a Canadian tax representative if the non-resident carries on business in Canada. The CRA issues the BN/RT account within 5-20 business days; the account must be quoted on all sales invoices, customs documents, and GST/HST returns. Authorization of an accountant or legal counsel is completed via Represent a Client (RAC) with the Business Number and CRA user ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada), a Business Corporation (Federal/Provincial) is a separate taxpayer filing a T2 corporate income tax return; no pass-through election exists. General federal Part I rate is 38% reduced by the 10% provincial abatement and general rate reduction to 15%; Alberta corporate income tax is 8% flat (2025). The small business deduction (9% federal on first CAD 500,000) is restricted to Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs), so a non-resident-controlled e-commerce entity generally pays the full 15% general federal rate plus 8% Alberta rate. GST/HST registration is a separate entity-level collection identity. Territorial scope: tax applies to supplies made in Canada, including imported digital and tangible supplies; exported goods and certain offshore services are zero-rated (Schedule VI, ETA). No tax-exempt zone regime exists in Alberta for e-commerce operators.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections relevant to this structure include: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration and streamlined non-resident registration (ETA s. 240(1)); (ii) functional currency election (ITA s. 261) permitting Canadian tax computations in USD; (iii) election to deem inventory sent cross-border to not be a taxable self-supply when goods remain owned by the vendor and move between Canadian and foreign jurisdictions; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.3 (draft rules applicable to taxation years beginning on or after October 1, 2025) disallow deductions on hybrid-financing and reverse-hybrid arrangements with no elective opt-out, though taxpayers may file structural re-characterization elections on prescribed forms; (v) Part I vs. Part XIV branch tax elections for non-resident insurers/carriers (not applicable to general retail); and (vi) GST/HST quick method election (ETA s. 226(1)) for eligible resident registrants, generally unavailable to non-residents, so full input tax credit (ITC) accounting is the default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act (ETA), administered by the CRA; Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax (PST), so the 5% federal GST is the sole indirect tax in CA-AB.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier exemption under ETA s. 148(1) when taxable supplies in Canada over four consecutive calendar quarters do not exceed CAD 30,000); mandatory registration for non-resident digital/e-commerce sellers and marketplace operators once taxable sales into Canada exceed CAD 30,000 per quarter, under the July 1, 2021 e-commerce supplier/marketplace regime (ETA s. 240(1.1) and associated distribution rules).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government API pre-clearance, or digital stamping for GST/HST invoices. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records if complete, legible, and retained for six years (ETA s. 286(1); IC-05-1). The Pan-Canadian business-to-business e-invoicing framework (Peppol PINT/UBL standard, administered by the Canadian Peppol Authority) is voluntary. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE for residents, GST/HST MEMO for non-residents), with monthly/quarterly remittance schedules based on revenue thresholds; third-party marketplace platforms (e.g., Amazon) must report seller data under the expanded GST/HST reporting regime and the new mandatory platform information reporting rules (CRA Information Return on Web Platforms) effective 2025.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported goods applies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, item 1 where the registrant supplies tangible personal property by way of sale and exports the goods in accordance with regulatory evidence requirements. For an Amazon FBA generalized retail operation, the Canadian registrant may zero-rate goods shipped from Alberta inventory to foreign Amazon fulfillment centers (US/EU/UK) provided: (i) title and risk pass to a non-resident purchaser or the goods are removed permanently from Canada; (ii) continuous and contemporaneous proof of export is maintained; and (iii) the goods are not in Canada at the time of the underlying consumer sale. Cross-border digital services and intangible supplies to non-residents may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, items 22-23, excluding services delivered to an individual physically present in Canada. Domestic Alberta FBA sales are subject to 5% GST; FBA deliveries into HST provinces (ON 13%, NS 15%, etc.) attract the destination province rate under place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA electronic B13A filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System - CERS, mandatory for exports valued over CAD 2,000; lower-value shipments evidenced by waybill and shipper's records)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / multimodal transport document showing origin in Alberta and foreign destination port/fulfillment center
Commercial Invoice and packing list in CAD with shipping terms (Incoterms), HS codes, and zero-rated status marker
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank wire/payment evidence from Amazon or foreign buyer matching export invoice value and currency)
Foreign fulfillment center receiving reports (Amazon shipment receipts, inbound delivery logs, pod records confirming arrival at US/EU warehouse)
ACI eManifest / PARS highway cargo control records for cross-border truck shipments and ocean/air Cargo Control Documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline in the ETA; the 180-day benchmark operates as the internal treasury and documentation protocol used to demonstrate a bona fide commercial export and is expressly referenced because CRA treats extended unrepatriated receivables as an indicator of off-book or non-export structuring. CRA audit triggers include persistent zero-rated refunds exceeding input tax credits, repetitive export claims with photocopied waybills, and shipments to foreign fulfillment centers without corresponding final consumer sale records. Penalties: (i) failure to register/remit (ETA s. 280) - CAD 250 simple; greater of CAD 250 and 25% of net tax if knowingly; (ii) gross negligence penalty (ETA s. 285) - 25% of the net tax falsely claimed; (iii) false statements and omissions (ETA s. 327.1) - CAD 2,500, or greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax for knowing conduct; (iv) criminal tax evasion (ETA ss. 327-333) - fines up to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment up to five years; (v) reassessment limitation extended beyond the standard four-year window to any period where misrepresentation is established (ETA s. 298); and (vi) retrospective clawback of all zero-rated amounts with interest compounded daily through arrears, together with denial of future refunds and public disclosure under CRA's Voluntary Disclosures Program only if disclosure precedes audit contact.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acts as the central monetary authority; however, Canada imposes no comprehensive foreign-exchange control regime. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) is the financial intelligence unit and AML/ATF supervisor under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. No separate government agency grants exchange-control permissions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for residents and non-residents under a freely floating exchange-rate system. There are no restrictions on profit remittances, dividend distributions, or repatriation of invested capital for an Alberta business corporation. Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to non-resident withholding tax of 25%, potentially reduced under applicable tax treaties (e.g., Canada-US Treaty may reduce to 5-15% depending on ownership levels). This withholding obligation is a revenue-collection measure only and does not limit the convertibility or transferability of funds. Transfers are subject to standard AML reporting thresholds but require no administrative authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose any statutory surrender requirement on export proceeds. Exporters are free to retain foreign currencies, hold receipts in offshore or onshore foreign-currency accounts, and are not bound by any conversion ratio or mandatory repatriation timeline. Export proceeds received through Canadian banks are subject to FINTRAC reporting when an international electronic funds transfer equals or exceeds CAD 10,000, and must be recorded for corporate income tax and GST/HST purposes, but no foreign-exchange surrender obligation exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operating Account (CAD/USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High with legal caveats. Cross-border electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Payoneer, and Stripe are widely used by Amazon FBA sellers and may lawfully hold funds for Canadian corporate clients. If an EMI provides money-services business (MSB) activities from within Canada, it must be registered with FINTRAC and may need provincial licensing in select provinces. Canadian corporations may maintain settlement accounts with offshore EMIs without breaching exchange controls, but they should not rely on an unregistered offshore EMI as the sole banking channel because it cannot provide Canadian-dollar clearing via ACSS or Lynx, nor direct payroll or tax remittance in CAD. Use of an EMI as a supplementary foreign-currency collection and disbursement layer is viable and common.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian schedule-I banks generally allow remote corporate account opening through video-identity verification and digital document submission, subject to the bank's risk appetite. Many banks still reserve the right to require an in-person interview at a branch or the engagement of a Canadian lawyer or notary to certify signatures and identify the ultimate beneficial owners. For an Alberta corporation with non-resident directors, standard practice involves a video-call identity check, written submission of passport and proof of address, corporate resolutions, certificate of incorporation, and a corporate register excerpt. Physical attendance is not universally mandatory, but some banks may impose a branch visit or notarized signature package for accounts involving non-Canadian signatories. Clearance should be obtained in advance from the business-banking officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated non-resident-owned corporation with no operating history and high projected marketplace revenue before the first corporate bank account is opened.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate of incorporation, articles and bylaws, notarized register of directors and shareholders, beneficial-ownership declaration, board resolution authorizing account opening, initial Amazon FBA marketplace registration proof, and a reference letter from the formation agent or home-jurisdiction bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume small-value deposits arriving from Amazon R2P settlement or other aggregated marketplace remittance platforms, generating continuous international electronic fund transfers above CAD 10,000 thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a signed compliance letter describing the Amazon FBA business model, Amazon settlement reports, product listing inventory summary, marketplace account ownership certificate, and a structured invoice/purchase-order ledger. Maintain all transfers through one named account to preserve a clear audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from a related foreign entity with layered beneficial-ownership structure and opaque source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete organizational chart showing all shareholding percentages, passport and proof-of-address for each ultimate beneficial owner above 10%, tax residency certificates, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, a written explanation of the source of injected funds, and where prudent, a Canadian legal opinion confirming the transaction is not suspicious.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders injecting equity or shareholder loans should route funds via SWIFT MT103 with the corporate account details, stating the purpose as 'contribution to share capital' or 'shareholder loan' in the payment narrative. For amounts at or above CAD 10,000, the remitting bank must identify the sender; the receiving Canadian bank will request a source-of-funds attestation and may complete a FINTRAC large international electronic transfer report. No government pre-approval is required for ordinary foreign direct investment; however, if the injection exceeds CAD 50 million, Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting is mandatory. Funds should be converted through the bank's FX desk only after arrival, using the corporate spot rate, and then credited to the CAD operating account via the ACSS for quick availability. For branch-controlled capital, an escrow account may be opened at BMO or RBC to hold funds until the corporation fulfills its statutory solvency requirement under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for FBA inventory procurement, freight, customs duties, and third-party charges may be executed via: (1) SWIFT MT103 wire for high-value international payments, including narrative purpose codes such as 'trade settlement' or 'commercial invoice payment'; (2) commercial letters of credit (L/C) where a supplier requires documentary guarantee, though open-account wire is preferred given FBA transaction velocity; (3) Canadian domestic clearing through ACSS for CAD disbursements and Lynx for real-time gross settlement of high-value interbank transfers; (4) dual-currency USD/CAD operating account structures permitting intercompany sweep into USD for U.S. supplier payments executed through Fedwire/CHIPS using the bank's U.S. correspondent network. FX conversion should be centralized with the corporate bank's online dealing platform to obtain interbank-like pricing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Direct deliverable forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) executed with a Canadian schedule-I bank or an authorized foreign bank branch under an ISDA or Canadian master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on CAD/CNY and CAD/BRL pairs to mitigate settlement risk where onshore delivery is unavailable
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY) between CAD and USD to hedge long-term capital-injection or liability exposure
Vanilla FX options (call/put) to protect against adverse currency movements for large one-off settlements
Zero-cost collar structures combining a forward with long and short options, permissible when hedged exposure is documented under IFRS 9 hedge accounting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each fiscal year end; anniversary of incorporation may apply if no fiscal year is established.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger late filing penalties and, after two consecutive missing annual returns, administrative dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires revival application and payment of outstanding fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year end; income tax balance of payment is due 2 months after year end (3 months for Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for small business deduction).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file timely faces a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, interest on outstanding balances, and possible prosecution for repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end for annual filers; daily/quarterly institutional periods per CRA determination.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of 6% of the unpaid amount plus 1% per month up to 12 months, plus statutory interest; milestone amounts may also trigger compliance audits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit applies to a private non-reporting corporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act unless requisitioned by shareholders holding not less than 10% of the issued shares, requested under the CBCA 5% rule if federal, or required under a special regulatory regime or by public securities rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Canadian GAAP: either IFRS (for publicly accountable enterprises) or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations; income reconciliation from GAAP to taxable income is required for CRA filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires maintenance of an ISC (Individuals with Significant Control) register, updated within 15 days of any share transfer or control change. The annual corporate secretarial process must include a directors' resolution confirming the ISC register's accuracy and the filing of the annual return that verifies registered office details and director information; no separate standalone public UBO filing is required under Alberta provincial law.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (federal Part I 15% after general rate reduction plus Alberta flat 8%); 11% combined rate for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) eligible for the federal small business deduction (9%) and Alberta small business deduction (2%) on the first C$500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal general rate reduction of 13%; federal small business deduction to 9% on up to C$500,000 active business income of a CCPC; Alberta small business deduction to 2%; SR&ED investment tax credits up to 35% of qualified expenditure; no provincial tax holidays in Alberta; Amazon FBA e-commerce net income is ordinary active business income assessed at the general combined rate when the corporation is not a CCPC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically through a CRA-certified E-file service provider or the CRA My Business Account portal; mandatory E-file applies to corporations with gross revenue exceeding C$1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal-period return; quarterly tax instalment remittances are required in advance where estimated Part I tax exceeds thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within six months after fiscal year-end; balance-due date is two months after year-end, extended to three months for a CCPC claiming the small business deduction; instalments are computed on prior-year, current-year, or graduated estimates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 1 – Legal Name and Registered Address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal corporate name, jurisdiction of incorporation (federal under CBCA or Alberta under BCA), and registered office address in Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name exactly as shown on the Alberta Corporate Registry or Corporations Canada record; maintain a valid Alberta registered office and, where required, Canadian resident directors; a non-resident may hold all shares but cannot convert the entity into a CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA-issued 9-digit business number linked to the corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply for a BN with the CRA before the first fiscal period; use the same BN for T2 filing, GST/HST returns on Amazon taxable sales, and any payroll account for Canadian employees or contractors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue; an Amazon FBA seller reports gross sales proceeds remitted by Amazon Marketplace, not the net deposit after referral, fulfillment, storage, and advertising deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue recognized by the Canadian-resident corporate seller; if the Canadian corporation acts as agent or commissionaire for a foreign principal, disclose the agency relationship and exclude pass-through principal revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Lines 200–299 – COGS, FBA Fees, Advertising and Fulfillment Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, Amazon referral fees, FBA fulfillment and storage fees, marketplace advertising spend, shipping, and other operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify intercompany purchases from related overseas suppliers are at arm's length; attach Form T106 and transfer-pricing documentation when aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceed C$1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income for tax purposes: net accounting income adjusted for non-deductible items, capital cost allowance, reserves, and loss carryovers; non-capital losses may be carried back three years and forward twenty years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable income to Alberta using the permanent-establishment formula on Schedule 4; a Canadian-resident corporation remains taxable on worldwide income and foreign tax credits are available only where a foreign permanent establishment or foreign-source income exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Part I Tax Calculation – Federal and Alberta Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal Part I tax at 38%, reduced by the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction to 15%, plus Alberta provincial tax at 8% on taxable income allocated to Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled Canadian corporation is not a CCPC and cannot claim the small business deduction; all treaty relief is claimed at the shareholder level on distributions, not on the T2.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months); repeat failure within a three-year window triggers 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20 months); late payment interest compounds daily at the CRA prescribed rate; gross negligence penalty is 50% of the understated tax under ITA s.163.2.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under ITA s.212(2) on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; no separate Alberta dividend withholding because Alberta corporate tax is federally administered under the Tax Collection Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the reduced DTA rate (commonly 5% to 15%, or 0% for qualifying pension or government entities): (1) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority; (2) deliver the TRC and any required CRA treaty-relief declaration (including Form NR301 or equivalent) to the paying Canadian corporation before the dividend is credited; (3) if tax is over-withheld, file a refund claim with the CRA International and Large Business Directorate within the applicable statutory period; (4) for tiered holding structures, substantiate the ultimate beneficial owner and satisfy the Limitation on Benefits or MLI principal-purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% on royalties under ITA s.212(1)(d) and generally 25% on interest under ITA s.212(1)(b), subject to the arm's-length portfolio interest exemption for interest to unrelated lenders; treaty rates: royalties commonly reduced to 10% (Canada–US Article XII, Canada–UK), and interest commonly reduced to 10–15% under major DTAs, with participation exemptions for interest to a corporate shareholder owning 10% or more of voting shares.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 – Form T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents) is mandatory when the aggregate annual value of reportable cross-border related-party transactions equals or exceeds C$1,000,000, or when outstanding related-party loans/indebtedness exceed C$1,000,000; contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation is legally expected above this threshold; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 (approximately C$1.1 billion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta and Canada do not apply Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style Economic Substance Regulations; equivalent safeguards operate through the central management and control residency test, the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s.245, including the 25% GAAR surcharge), and substance-over-form recharacterization; an Amazon FBA shell corporation with no Canadian office, employees, or board decision-making power is exposed to (a) reassessment of income to the real economic owner and (b) denial of treaty benefits under the OECD MLI principal-purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False or Omitted Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting Amazon Marketplace gross revenue, inflating FBA fees or inventory cost of goods sold, destroying seller central records, or concealing foreign-related entities and accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of tax plus compounded interest; criminal fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment (up to 2 years on summary conviction) under ITA s.239(1); civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under ITA s.163.2; additional late-filing penalties of 5% to 20%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or acquiesce in false returns commit an offence; Canadian courts may pierce the corporate veil for fraudulent conduct; CRA can pursue personal garnishment and restitution orders; tax debts above C$50,000 can trigger passport denial or revocation procedures; directors also face civil fiduciary claims from the corporate estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form T106, absence of contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, intercompany payments to a foreign parent or Amazon-related service provider at non-arm's-length margins, or unilateral use of unreasonable TP methods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty on the net transfer-pricing adjustment under ITA s.247(3); T106 late-filing and failure penalties in addition to reassessment; disallowance of expense deductions and corresponding interest on deficient instalments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatic insurers of transfer-pricing accuracy, but personal liability attaches where they knowingly sign false documentation; CRA may assert secondary liability under ITA s.160 against shareholders or directors who receive diverted corporate value; criminal exposure arises if TP manipulation is part of a fraudulent tax-evasion scheme.
